## Phase Goal

Verbatim from `.planning/ROADMAP.md` §Phase 5. Not in `As a … I want to … so that …` form and not
rewritten here — run `/gsd mvp-phase 5` if the three-slot form is wanted.

> The night runs past the draft — round robin, a seeded cut, a single-elimination bracket, results
> recorded and correctable — and the finished tournament stays readable and re-runnable after the
> Champions roster rotates

**Slice delivered by this plan:** the app can hold more than one regulation at once and can reach a
newer one. This is the half of the roster story that has no UI yet — 05-07 puts the two controls and
the banner on the config screen — but it is the half where the mechanism lives, and it is the only
place in the phase where something was genuinely unknown before research probed it.

<precedence>
`05-UI-SPEC.md:44` states "There is no `05-RESEARCH.md`." It is dated a day earlier. **RESEARCH
governs mechanism; UI-SPEC governs copy, layout and tokens.** This plan is mechanism; the sentences
a host reads are 05-07's and come from `05-UI-SPEC.md` §2 byte-for-byte.

**Transport ruling: same-origin.** Both documents reach it. The deciding reason is RESEARCH's, not
the CONTEXT's: `raw.githubusercontent.com` serves this repo's `roster.index.json` with
`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` and would need no service-worker change at all — but it **cannot
bring sprites**, because 300-plus PNGs are not fetched from `raw`, so it cannot deliver a *usable*
new regulation. The `roster-source.ts:1-13` invariant is preserved as a consequence rather than as
the reason.

**RESEARCH Correction 1, which changes what this plan must not do:** `05-CONTEXT.md` §Discretion
says the T-01-25 invariant is "stated in the code **and asserted by a test**". It is not. `T-01-25`
appears in `01-05-PLAN.md`, `01-05-SUMMARY.md` and the `roster-source.ts:9` doc block, and there is
no test anywhere referencing `loadRoster`, `RosterLoadError` or a third-party origin. Do not search
for a test to update. **This plan creates the module's first test file**; adding a same-origin
assertion to it is a genuine improvement rather than a restoration.
</precedence>

<objective>
Turn `roster-source.ts` from "the module that resolves the roster" into "the module that resolves
any of the rosters this build knows about, and can go and get a newer one."

Purpose: D-24 makes a tournament's roster a settled fact — `config.rosterVersion` and
`rosterChecksum` already pin it and ROST-06 already keeps `public/data/roster.ma.json` committed —
but `loadRoster()` resolves exactly one regulation, so the app cannot currently honour the pin. And
`parseSnapshot` deliberately skips per-row validation with a stated reason that does not survive
contact with REFR-02: the file is no longer a committed artifact produced by a tested transform, it
is whatever the host chose in a file picker.

Output: a snapshot registry, a strict parser shared by both refresh paths, and the module's first
tests.
</objective>

// src/adapters/roster-source.ts
export interface SnapshotIndexEntry {
  id: string;
  label: string;
  json: string;          // still gated by SNAPSHOT_FILE_PATTERN
  validFrom: string;     // YYYY-MM-DD — newly carried
  validUntil: string;    // YYYY-MM-DD — newly carried, REFR-03 reads it
  checksum: string;      // newly carried, the already-current check reads it
  counts: { draftable: number; megaCapable: number };
}

export async function loadRoster(regulationId?: string): Promise<RosterBundle>;

/** Registry read. `null` when this build has never resolved that regulation. D-24. */
export function resolveSnapshot(rosterVersion: string): RosterBundle | null;

export type RefreshOutcome =
  | { kind: 'alreadyCurrent'; label: string }
  | { kind: 'updated'; label: string; validUntil: string }
  | { kind: 'failed' };
export async function refreshRoster(): Promise<RefreshOutcome>;

/** REFR-02. Same validator as the fetch path, no network. */
export async function readRosterFile(file: File): Promise<RosterBundle | null>;

  <action>
Widen `parseIndex` to carry `validFrom`, `validUntil`, `checksum` and `counts`, refusing an entry
that is missing any of them. Keep `SNAPSHOT_FILE_PATTERN` gating `json` and keep its comment — it is
the reason a string from data can never become an arbitrary URL, and this plan adds a second fetch
path that depends on it. Note in the doc block which consumer needs which new field: REFR-03 reads
`validUntil`, the already-current check reads `checksum`, and `counts` is the cross-check
`parseSnapshotStrict` uses.

Add `parseSnapshotStrict` **beside** `parseSnapshot`, not instead of it, and put the reason for the
split in its own doc block. `parseSnapshot`'s exemption is stated at `:129-139` and is sound for its
input: the file is generated by a tested pure transform and pinned by
`tests/core/roster/fixtures.test.ts`, so re-validating 235 rows on every page load would cost more
than it proves. REFR-02's input is a file a host chose in a picker, and REFR-01's has crossed the
network; neither is that.

Implement the six checks from RESEARCH §Validation, rebuilding field by field on `buildPlayers`'s
model rather than casting. Reuse `POISON_KEYS`' posture for own-property refusal, and `JSON.parse`
without a reviver on both paths.

**Do not recompute the SHA-256**, and write the three-part argument into the doc block so nobody
adds it later: the checksum is *self-declared* by the file, so recomputing proves internal
consistency rather than authenticity — which the structural checks above already prove more cheaply;
it would require shipping `canonicalJson`, which today exists only in `scripts/build-roster.mjs`;
and `crypto.subtle` is **undefined outside a secure context**, the exact case `src/adapters/id.ts:9-14`
already worries about ("a phone opening the host's laptop over `http://192.168.x.x`"). A verification
step that silently cannot run on that deployment is worse than none. The checksum stays an
*identity* value, which is what `config.rosterChecksum` and `pool/built.checksum` already use it for.

Create `tests/adapters/roster-source.test.ts` — the module's first test file. Give it a header
stating that it exists partly because RESEARCH Correction 1 found the T-01-25 invariant had no test
at all. Add a rejection table with one case per `<behavior>` rejection bullet, plus an acceptance
case built from a trimmed but structurally faithful copy of the committed snapshot shape.

  <behavior>
    - `refreshRoster()` fetches `data/roster.index.json?refresh=1` with `{ cache: 'reload',
      credentials: 'omit' }`.
    - When the fetched index's default regulation and `checksum` match the currently resolved
      snapshot's, it returns `{ kind: 'alreadyCurrent' }` and issues **no** further request.
    - When they differ, it fetches the named snapshot (and `sprite-meta.json` when the new regulation
      adds species), runs `parseSnapshotStrict`, adopts the result into the registry as the new
      default, and returns `{ kind: 'updated', label, validUntil }`.
    - A `fetch` rejection, a non-`ok` response, or a `parseSnapshotStrict` refusal all return
      `{ kind: 'failed' }` and leave the registry exactly as it was.
    - The already-current comparison uses `checksum` and `regulation`. **No comparison anywhere reads
      a byte count, a `Content-Length`, or a string length.**
    - Every URL this module builds still starts with `import.meta.env.BASE_URL` and every fetched
      filename still passes `SNAPSHOT_FILE_PATTERN`.
    - `readRosterFile(file)` parses through the same `parseSnapshotStrict`, issues no request at all,
      returns the bundle on success and `null` on any refusal.
    - `readRosterFile` refuses a file over the existing size gate before reading it.
  </behavior>

  <action>
Add `const REFRESH_MARKER = '?refresh=1'` with RESEARCH's doc block verbatim — the `?refresh` marker
is what `public/sw.js` looks for to step aside, `cache: 'reload'` is what steps past the HTTP cache
Pages sets to `max-age=600`, and **both are required and neither is sufficient**: a service worker
intercepts a `reload` request like any other, and `ignoreSearch: true` makes the query alone
invisible to the cache lookup.

Write `refreshRoster()` as RESEARCH's four steps. Step 2 returns early on a checksum-and-regulation
match, and that early return is the common case and the reason the whole operation is usually one
1.8 KB request — say so.

Put Pitfall 7's finding in a comment at the comparison site: the local checkout has CRLF and the
deployed file has LF, so `roster.mb.json` is 147,021 bytes on disk and 140,170 on the origin with an
**identical** checksum. Any length or byte-equality comparison reports a change on every Windows
checkout forever and never on CI. The checksum is computed over `canonicalJson(entries)` from parsed
values and is line-ending independent.

Add the sprites-and-offline paragraph to the refresh doc block: a refreshed regulation adds species
whose PNGs are on the origin but not in the current precache, so offline those rows fall back to
`_placeholder.png` via `handleSpriteError`. That is a stated, accepted degradation and it must be
written down here rather than discovered as a bug later.

Write `readRosterFile(file)` over `file-io.readJsonFile`'s size gate, routing the parsed value
through the **same** `parseSnapshotStrict`. One validator, two entry points — a second one would be
free to disagree about what a roster is. It issues no request, which is REFR-02's entire point and
the reason the refresh failure sentence names it.

Update the module header at `:1-13`: the "no third-party origin is contacted at runtime (T-01-25)"
invariant **stays** and gains a paragraph about `?refresh=1` — what the marker is for, that the
worker looks for it, and that offline the request fails and that failure is correct because REFR-02
is the alternative. Do not weaken the invariant sentence.

Extend the test file with a case per `<behavior>` bullet, including a failing-fetch case asserting
the registry is unchanged, and an explicit assertion that every URL the stub was called with begins
with the base URL and contains no other origin.
  </action>

## Trust Boundaries

| Boundary | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| the network → `parseSnapshotStrict` | A fetched snapshot has crossed a boundary the committed one never did. |
| a host's file picker → `parseSnapshotStrict` | REFR-02's input is whatever the host chose. This is the phase's most clearly untrusted input after the tournament JSON. |
| a string from data → a URL | `SNAPSHOT_FILE_PATTERN` is the gate that stops "a filename from the index" becoming "an arbitrary URL". |
| a `rosterVersion` on a document → the registry | A document can name a regulation this build has never heard of. |

## STRIDE Threat Register

| Threat ID | Category | Component | Disposition | Mitigation Plan |
|-----------|----------|-----------|-------------|-----------------|
| T-05-14 | Tampering | a malicious or corrupt roster JSON from the file picker (REFR-02) | mitigate | `parseSnapshotStrict` rebuilds field by field on `buildPlayers`'s allow-list model, checks per-row shape, unique ids, `counts.draftable === entries.length`, ISO date shapes and a non-empty checksum, and refuses `POISON_KEYS` as own properties. `JSON.parse` runs with no reviver. `file-io.readJsonFile`'s size gate runs before the read. |
| T-05-15 | Tampering | prototype pollution through the roster path | mitigate | Own-property refusal for `__proto__`, `constructor` and `prototype`, reusing `import-guard.ts`'s posture, applied on both the fetch and the file path because they share one validator. Pinned by a dedicated test. |
| T-05-16 | Tampering / SSRF-analogue | a data-supplied filename interpolated into a fetch URL | mitigate | `SNAPSHOT_FILE_PATTERN` still gates every `json` value from the index, `SPRITE_FILE_PATTERN` still gates sprite filenames, and `REFRESH_MARKER` is a fixed literal that is never interpolated. Every URL is `import.meta.env.BASE_URL` plus a fixed template, asserted by a test over the fetch stub's arguments. |
| T-05-17 | Spoofing | a third-party origin serving the roster | mitigate | Same-origin only, `credentials: 'omit'` stated explicitly rather than inherited from the default. `grep -c "raw.githubusercontent.com"` returning 0 is an acceptance criterion, and the module's first test file adds the same-origin assertion RESEARCH Correction 1 found was missing. |
| T-05-18 | Tampering | a `?refresh=1` request used as a general precache bypass | mitigate | Bounded in 05-02 by the worker's return ordering. On this side, only `refreshRoster` ever appends the marker, it is a module constant, and no caller supplies it — so the bypass reaches exactly three fixed same-origin JSON paths. |
| T-05-19 | Repudiation | silently substituting a roster for one a document names | mitigate | `resolveSnapshot` returns `null` and never falls back. A completed tournament is never rendered against a roster that could not have contained its picks; the caller states the problem and offers REFR-02 as the recovery, reusing `app.tsx`'s existing `rosterDriftNotice` surface. |
| T-05-20 | Denial of service | a refresh that reports a change on every developer machine forever | mitigate | The comparison reads `checksum` and `regulation`, never bytes or lengths. Pitfall 7's CRLF finding is written at the comparison site and a `grep` acceptance criterion pins the absence of any size comparison. |
| T-05-SC | Tampering | npm/pip/cargo installs | accept | This plan installs nothing; `package.json` is not modified. |
</threat_model>
